messages:
Tess Howard (AE): Heads-up 11 NimbusVault sent an RFI this morning. Main asks: capability matrix, short perf numbers for a 16k POC, autoscale behaviour under burst, BYOK/HSM wording, and three POC pricing options (hosted, small dedicated, private+HSM). Can eng/security/billing help?

Ravi Singh (SSE): I can draft the matrix. Quick clarifier: do they need 16k everywhere or occasional 32k? That changes p95 considerably.

Tess Howard (AE): They said primary 16k, occasional 32k for long reports. Target POC: 160 concurrent gen streams, 35k embed/day, EU-only tenancy.

Ivan Petrov (Eng-ML): Draft matrix for RFI table below. Keep numbers conservative and call out assumptions.

Ivan Petrov (Eng-ML): ```
Capability | Hosted API | Dedicated (small) | Private (VPC + HSM / BYOK)
---------- | ---------: | -----------------: | ----------------------------
Context support | up to 32k (model dep) | up to 32k | up to 32k
Gen p50 (16k) | 120-200 ms | 80-130 ms | 90-150 ms
Gen p95 (16k) | 480-800 ms | 300-520 ms | 320-560 ms
Gen p50 (32k) | 420-680 ms | 280-420 ms | 300-480 ms
Embed p50 | 30-70 ms | 15-40 ms | 20-45 ms
Concurrency handling | bursty (soft limits) | reserved pools (predictable) | customer pools (configurable)
Autoscale behaviour | autoscale with cold-starts; best-effort EU nodes | pre-warmed nodes for reserved pools | customer-controlled scaling
Caching | automatic prefix/KV caching | tuned caching + reserved KV | local cache + KV in VPC
Quantization | bf16 / int8 | int8 recommended for reserved | int8 + custom kernels
KMS/HSM | Redwood KMS | customer KMS integ | customer HSM / BYOK (add-on)
SLA | standard | SLA-backed | enterprise SLA
```

Clara Mendes (Security): Approved HSM/BYOK wording for RFI: "Customer-managed HSM or HSM-backed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. Keys used for encryption, signing, and audit remain in customer-controlled hardware; Redwood control plane never receives plaintext keys. We can provide attestation and key lifecycle artifacts under NDA." Legal will gate SOC2/ISO attachments.

Ravi Singh (SSE): Ops blurb to add: "Autoscale notes: Hosted autoscale favors availability; cold-starts may increase p95 temporarily. Dedicated reserved pools can be pre-warmed to avoid cold-start latency. For EU-only tenancy, failover and burst capacity are restricted to EU regions; customers may opt into cross-region burst for additional capacity. We support configurable fallback policies: queue/backpressure, route to compatible quantized variants, or route to hosted EU-compatible pool (if tenant not pinned)."

Ivan Petrov (Eng-ML): Add note on performance assumptions: "Latency ranges assume 16k working set, baseline bf16 model family, moderate batching tuned for p95 targets, and enabled prefix/KV caching for retrieval patterns. Int8 quant reduces cost but can increase variance; Private deployments can leverage custom kernel tuning to improve int8 p95."

billing-bot: Preliminary POC estimates uploaded: hosted (10-day) unoptimized ~ $11,200, optimized ~$4,200; small dedicated (10-day reserved) ~$20,500; Private EU + HSM (10-day) starting ~$36,000 + integration fee ~$7,500. Margins and final FX pending finance review.

Clara Mendes (Security): Data residency and logs: "Dedicated and Private can be pinned to EU-only tenancy. Hosted API can be restricted to EU regions but is not air-gapped by default. Logs retention configurable; default 30 days."

Tess Howard (AE): Can we aim to have a polished RFI bundle (matrix + 3 short Q&A bullets for each ask + pricing rows + HSM wording + ops blurb) by tomorrow EOD? Ravi, take matrix + draft answers; Clara finalize security lines; Ivan a one-paragraph perf note; billing-bot confirm final numbers with finance.

Ravi Singh (SSE): On it. I'll post a draft here by 15:00 CET.

Ivan Petrov (Eng-ML): I'll paste the perf paragraph by 13:00 CET.

Clara Mendes (Security): I'll flag any legal gating items inline once draft appears.

Tess Howard (AE): Thanks team :rocket:
